newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania starts restructuring of mining sector.
newsitem.headline: Romania starts restructuring of mining sector.

text.p: Romania has launched a programme to restructure its oversized and loss-making mining sector, involving layoffs and the dismantling of state-run companies, the Industry Minister said on Wednesday.
"Our plan is to streamline the sector, cut losses, phase out subsidies and close the mines where costs significantly outrun the value of their output," Calin Tariceanu said.

Under the programme, the state-controlled companies running the lignite mines in the Oltenia region and the central area of Ploiesti as well as lead and zinc mines in Baia Mare, in northwest Romania, would be dismantled and part of them turned into commercial companies, he told Reuters.
The state companies, which also include the big utilities, are responsible for the bulk of the losses in Romania's economy.
"The units which now perform transport, repair and maintenance services will be separated at those mines and will work for the sector on a commercial bases," Tariceanu said.

More than 4,000 jobs would be cut at the Ploiesti and Baia Mare mines, he said, adding that many of the staff made redundant had actually asked to leave the sector in exchange for cash handouts amounting to up to 12 average monthly wages.
Separate restructuring programmes for the troubled hard coal mines in the western Jiu Valley and for the non-ferrous ore mines would be presented by the ministry later this month.
Last month, the miners in the Jiu Valley -- notorious for their violent anti-reform riots in the early 1990s --, staged a 10-day strike demanding a 45 percent wage increase.

Tariceanu said the ministry was considering projects to minimise the social coasts of reforms in the mono-industrial coalbasins. Deveolpment of the farming, wood and tourism sectors in those areas could absorb part of the unemployed.
Losses in the mining sector, affected by inefficiency and bad management, amounted to 621 billion lei in 1996, data show. The ministry hopes to cut this figure by 50 percent in 1997.
"We can't afford to keep in operation mines where production costs exceed up to eight times the value of the extracted product. We are rich in poor resources," he said.
Romania's coal mines are not economically competitive. Hard coal pits have a complex geological structure, with a high content of dust and methane.
The restructuring project would keep coal output at the 34 million tonnes expected this year. Of this, 30 million tonnes will be lignite and four million tonnes hard coal, a ministry official said.
"Romania will not resort to coal imports. Actually, the energy sector has an excess of coal in stock," said.
